differences.authoritative: Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in His hands? Who has bound up the waters in His cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is the name of His Son—surely you know!

differences.structured: Every word of God is flawless;He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
differences.authoritative: Every word of God is flawless; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.

differences.structured: Do not add to His words,lest He rebuke you and prove you a liar.
differences.authoritative: Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and prove you a liar.

differences.structured: Two things I ask of You —do not refuse me before I die:
differences.authoritative: Two things I ask of You—do not refuse me before I die:

differences.structured: Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me.Give me neither poverty nor riches;feed me with the bread that is my portion.
differences.authoritative: Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread that is my portion.

differences.structured: Otherwise, I may have too muchand deny You, saying, ‘Who is the LORD?’Or I may become poor and steal,profaning the name of my God.
differences.authoritative: Otherwise, I may have too much and deny You, saying, ‘Who is the LORD?’ Or I may become poor and steal, profaning the name of my God.

differences.structured: Do not slander a servant to his master,or he will curse you, and you will bear the guilt.
differences.authoritative: Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will bear the guilt.

differences.structured: There is a generation of those who curse their fathersand do not bless their mothers.
differences.authoritative: There is a generation of those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.

differences.structured: There is a generation of those who are pure in their own eyesand yet unwashed of their filth.
differences.authoritative: There is a generation of those who are pure in their own eyes and yet unwashed of their filth.

differences.structured: There is a generation— how haughty are their eyesand pretentious are their glances —
differences.authoritative: There is a generation—how haughty are their eyes and pretentious are their glances—

differences.structured: there is a generation whose teeth are swordsand whose jaws are knives,devouring the oppressed from the earthand the needy from among men.
differences.authoritative: there is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, devouring the oppressed from the earth and the needy from among men.

differences.structured: The leech has two daughters:Give and Give.There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, ‘Enough!’:
differences.authoritative: The leech has two daughters: Give and Give. There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, ‘Enough!’:

differences.structured: Sheol,the barren womb,land never satisfied with water,and fire that never says, ‘Enough!’
differences.authoritative: Sheol, the barren womb, land never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, ‘Enough!’

differences.structured: As for the eye that mocks a fatherand scorns obedience to a mother,may the ravens of the valley pluck it outand young vultures devour it.
differences.authoritative: As for the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother, may the ravens of the valley pluck it out and young vultures devour it.

differences.structured: the way of an eagle in the sky,the way of a snake on a rock,the way of a ship at sea,and the way of a man with a maiden.
differences.authoritative: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship at sea, and the way of a man with a maiden.

differences.structured: This is the way of an adulteress:She eats and wipes her mouthand says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’
differences.authoritative: This is the way of an adulteress: She eats and wipes her mouth and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’

differences.structured: a servant who becomes king,a fool who is filled with food,
differences.authoritative: a servant who becomes king, a fool who is filled with food,

differences.structured: an unloved woman who marries,and a maidservant who supplants her mistress.
differences.authoritative: an unloved woman who marries, and a maidservant who supplants her mistress.

differences.structured: a strutting rooster;a he-goat;and a king with his army around him.
differences.authoritative: a strutting rooster; a he-goat; and a king with his army around him.

differences.structured: If you have foolishly exalted yourselfor if you have plotted evil,put your hand over your mouth.
differences.authoritative: If you have foolishly exalted yourself or if you have plotted evil, put your hand over your mouth.

differences.structured: For as the churning of milk yields butter,and the twisting of the nose draws blood,so the stirring of anger brings forth strife.”
differences.authoritative: For as the churning of milk yields butter, and the twisting of the nose draws blood, so the stirring of anger brings forth strife.”

differences.structured: These are the words of King Lemuel — the burden that his mother taught him:
differences.authoritative: These are the words of King Lemuel—the burden that his mother taught him:

differences.structured: What shall I say, O my son?What, O son of my womb?What, O son of my vows?
differences.authoritative: What shall I say, O my son? What, O son of my womb? What, O son of my vows?

differences.structured: Do not spend your strength on womenor your vigor on those who ruin kings.
differences.authoritative: Do not spend your strength on women or your vigor on those who ruin kings.

differences.structured: It is not for kings, O Lemuel,it is not for kings to drink wine,or for rulers to crave strong drink,
differences.authoritative: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, or for rulers to crave strong drink,

differences.structured: lest they drink and forget what is decreed,depriving all the oppressed of justice.
differences.authoritative: lest they drink and forget what is decreed, depriving all the oppressed of justice.

differences.structured: Give strong drink to one who is perishing,and wine to the bitter in soul.
differences.authoritative: Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to the bitter in soul.

differences.structured: Let him drink and forget his poverty,and remember his misery no more.
differences.authoritative: Let him drink and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.

differences.structured: Open your mouth for those with no voice,for the cause of all the dispossessed.
differences.authoritative: Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed.

differences.structured: Open your mouth, judge righteously,and defend the cause of the poor and needy.
differences.authoritative: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy.

differences.structured: A wife of noble character, who can find?She is far more precious than rubies.
differences.authoritative: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.

differences.structured: The heart of her husband trusts in her,and he lacks nothing of value.
differences.authoritative: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he lacks nothing of value.

differences.structured: She brings him good and not harmall the days of her life.
differences.authoritative: She brings him good and not harm all the days of her life.

differences.structured: She selects wool and flaxand works with eager hands.
differences.authoritative: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands.

differences.structured: She is like the merchant ships,bringing her food from afar.
differences.authoritative: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.

differences.structured: She rises while it is still nightto provide food for her householdand portions for her maidservants.
differences.authoritative: She rises while it is still night to provide food for her household and portions for her maidservants.

differences.structured: She appraises a field and buys it;from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
differences.authoritative: She appraises a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.

differences.structured: She girds herself with strengthand shows that her arms are strong.
differences.authoritative: She girds herself with strength and shows that her arms are strong.

differences.structured: She sees that her gain is good,and her lamp is not extinguished at night.
differences.authoritative: She sees that her gain is good, and her lamp is not extinguished at night.

differences.structured: She stretches out her hands to the distaffand grasps the spindle with her fingers.
differences.authoritative: She stretches out her hands to the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers.

differences.structured: She opens her arms to the poorand reaches out her hands to the needy.
differences.authoritative: She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.

differences.structured: When it snows, she has no fear for her household,for they are all clothed in scarlet.
differences.authoritative: When it snows, she has no fear for her household, for they are all clothed in scarlet.

differences.structured: She makes coverings for her bed;her clothing is fine linen and purple.
differences.authoritative: She makes coverings for her bed; her clothing is fine linen and purple.

differences.structured: Her husband is known at the city gates,where he sits among the elders of the land.
differences.authoritative: Her husband is known at the city gates, where he sits among the elders of the land.

differences.structured: She makes linen garments and sells them;she delivers sashes to the merchants.
differences.authoritative: She makes linen garments and sells them; she delivers sashes to the merchants.

differences.structured: Strength and honor are her clothing,and she can laugh at the days to come.
differences.authoritative: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.

differences.structured: She opens her mouth with wisdom,and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
differences.authoritative: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.

differences.structured: She watches over the affairs of her householdand does not eat the bread of idleness.
differences.authoritative: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.

differences.structured: Her children rise up and call her blessed;her husband praises her as well:
differences.authoritative: Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her as well:

differences.structured: “Many daughters have done noble things,but you surpass them all!”
differences.authoritative: “Many daughters have done noble things, but you surpass them all!”

differences.structured: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting,but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
differences.authoritative: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.

differences.structured: Give her the fruit of her hands,and let her works praise her at the gates.
differences.authoritative: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.

differences.structured: “Futility of futilities,”says the Teacher,“futility of futilities!Everything is futile!”
differences.authoritative: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”

differences.structured: What does a man gain from all his labor,at which he toils under the sun?
differences.authoritative: What does a man gain from all his labor, at which he toils under the sun?

differences.structured: Generations come and generations go,but the earth remains forever.
differences.authoritative: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.

differences.structured: The sun rises and the sun sets;it hurries back to where it rises.
differences.authoritative: The sun rises and the sun sets; it hurries back to where it rises.

differences.structured: The wind blows southward,then turns northward;round and round it swirls,ever returning on its course.
differences.authoritative: The wind blows southward, then turns northward; round and round it swirls, ever returning on its course.

differences.structured: All the rivers flow into the sea,yet the sea is never full;to the place from which the streams come,there again they flow.
differences.authoritative: All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place from which the streams come, there again they flow.

differences.structured: All things are wearisome,more than one can describe;the eye is not satisfied with seeing,nor the ear content with hearing.
differences.authoritative: All things are wearisome, more than one can describe; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear content with hearing.

differences.structured: What has been will be again,and what has been done will be done again;there is nothing new under the sun.
differences.authoritative: What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.

differences.structured: Is there a case where one can say,“Look, this is new”?It has already existedin the ages before us.
differences.authoritative: Is there a case where one can say, “Look, this is new”? It has already existed in the ages before us.

differences.structured: There is no remembranceof those who came before,and those yet to come will not be rememberedby those who follow after.
differences.authoritative: There is no remembrance of those who came before, and those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow after.

differences.structured: What is crooked cannot be straightened,and what is lacking cannot be counted.
differences.authoritative: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.

differences.structured: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow,and as knowledge grows, grief increases.
differences.authoritative: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and as knowledge grows, grief increases.

differences.structured: I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good!”But it proved to be futile.
differences.authoritative: I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good!” But it proved to be futile.

differences.structured: I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly— my mind still guiding me with wisdom— until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.
differences.authoritative: I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom—until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.

differences.structured: and I accumulated for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I gathered to myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men — many concubines.
differences.authoritative: and I accumulated for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I gathered to myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men—many concubines.

differences.structured: The wise man has eyes in his head,but the fool walks in darkness.Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.
differences.authoritative: The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.

differences.structured: So I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will also befall me. What then have I gained by being wise?”And I said to myself that this too is futile.
differences.authoritative: So I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will also befall me. What then have I gained by being wise?” And I said to myself that this too is futile.

differences.structured: To everything there is a season,and a time for every purpose under heaven:
differences.authoritative: To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:

differences.structured: a time to be born and a time to die,a time to plant and a time to uproot,
differences.authoritative: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot,

differences.structured: a time to kill and a time to heal,a time to break down and a time to build,
differences.authoritative: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build,

differences.structured: a time to weep and a time to laugh,a time to mourn and a time to dance,
differences.authoritative: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,

differences.structured: a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together,a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,
differences.authoritative: a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,

differences.structured: a time to search and a time to count as lost,a time to keep and a time to discard,
differences.authoritative: a time to search and a time to count as lost, a time to keep and a time to discard,

differences.structured: a time to tear and a time to mend,a time to be silent and a time to speak,
differences.authoritative: a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak,

differences.structured: a time to love and a time to hate,a time for war and a time for peace.
differences.authoritative: a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.

differences.structured: and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor — this is the gift of God.
differences.authoritative: and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.

differences.structured: For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other — they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.
differences.authoritative: For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other—they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.

differences.structured: The fool folds his handsand consumes his own flesh.
differences.authoritative: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.

differences.structured: Better one handful with tranquilitythan two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.
differences.authoritative: Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.

differences.structured: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile — a miserable task.
differences.authoritative: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.

differences.structured: As a dream comes through many cares,so the speech of a fool comes with many words.
differences.authoritative: As a dream comes through many cares, so the speech of a fool comes with many words.

differences.structured: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him — for this is his lot.
differences.authoritative: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him—for this is his lot.

differences.structured: All a man’s labor is for his mouth,yet his appetite is never satisfied.
differences.authoritative: All a man’s labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.

differences.structured: For the more words, the more futility — and how does that profit anyone?
differences.authoritative: For the more words, the more futility—and how does that profit anyone?

differences.structured: A good name is better than fine perfume,and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.
differences.authoritative: A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.

differences.structured: It is better to enter a house of mourningthan a house of feasting,since death is the end of every man,and the living should take this to heart.
differences.authoritative: It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, since death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.

differences.structured: Sorrow is better than laughter,for a sad countenance is good for the heart.
differences.authoritative: Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance is good for the heart.

differences.structured: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning,but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
differences.authoritative: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.

differences.structured: It is better to heed a wise man’s rebukethan to listen to the song of fools.
differences.authoritative: It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.

differences.structured: For like the crackling of thorns under the pot,so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.
differences.authoritative: For like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.

differences.structured: Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool,and a bribe corrupts the heart.
differences.authoritative: Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.

differences.structured: The end of a matter is better than the beginning,and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.
differences.authoritative: The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.

differences.structured: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit,for anger settles in the lap of a fool.
differences.authoritative: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of a fool.

differences.structured: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?”For it is unwise of you to ask about this.
differences.authoritative: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.

differences.structured: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good,and it benefits those who see the sun.
differences.authoritative: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good, and it benefits those who see the sun.

differences.structured: For wisdom, like money, is a shelter,and the advantage of knowledgeis that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
differences.authoritative: For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.

differences.structured: Consider the work of God:Who can straighten what He has bent?
differences.authoritative: Consider the work of God: Who can straighten what He has bent?

differences.structured: In the day of prosperity, be joyful,but in the day of adversity, consider this:God has made one of these along with the other,so that a man cannot discoveranything that will come after him.
differences.authoritative: In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover anything that will come after him.

differences.structured: In my futile life I have seen both of these:A righteous man perishing in his righteousness,and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.
differences.authoritative: In my futile life I have seen both of these: A righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.

differences.structured: Wisdom makes the wise manstronger than ten rulers in a city.
differences.authoritative: Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city.

differences.structured: Surely there is no righteous man on earthwho does good and never sins.
differences.authoritative: Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.

differences.structured: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth — though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night —
differences.authoritative: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth—though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night—

differences.structured: Let your garments always be white,and never spare the oil for your head.
differences.authoritative: Let your garments always be white, and never spare the oil for your head.

differences.structured: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun — all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.
differences.authoritative: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.

differences.structured: The calm words of the wise are heededover the shouts of a ruler among fools.
differences.authoritative: The calm words of the wise are heeded over the shouts of a ruler among fools.

differences.structured: Wisdom is better than weapons of war,but one sinner destroys much good.
differences.authoritative: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

differences.structured: As dead flies bring a stench to the perfumer’s oil,so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
differences.authoritative: As dead flies bring a stench to the perfumer’s oil, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.

differences.structured: A wise man’s heart inclines to the right,but the heart of a fool to the left.
differences.authoritative: A wise man’s heart inclines to the right, but the heart of a fool to the left.

differences.structured: Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking,and he shows everyone that he is a fool.
differences.authoritative: Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.

differences.structured: If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post,for calmness lays great offenses to rest.
differences.authoritative: If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.

differences.structured: There is an evil I have seen under the sun —an error that proceeds from the ruler:
differences.authoritative: There is an evil I have seen under the sun—an error that proceeds from the ruler:

differences.structured: Folly is appointed to great heights,but the rich sit in lowly positions.
differences.authoritative: Folly is appointed to great heights, but the rich sit in lowly positions.

differences.structured: I have seen slaves on horseback,while princes go on foot like slaves.
differences.authoritative: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.

differences.structured: He who digs a pit may fall into it,and he who breaches a wall may be bitten by a snake.
differences.authoritative: He who digs a pit may fall into it, and he who breaches a wall may be bitten by a snake.

differences.structured: The one who quarries stones may be injured by them,and he who splits logs endangers himself.
differences.authoritative: The one who quarries stones may be injured by them, and he who splits logs endangers himself.

differences.structured: If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened,more strength must be exerted,but skill produces success.
differences.authoritative: If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened, more strength must be exerted, but skill produces success.

differences.structured: If the snake bites before it is charmed,there is no profit for the charmer.
differences.authoritative: If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.

differences.structured: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious,but the lips of a fool consume him.
differences.authoritative: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.

differences.structured: The beginning of his talk is folly,and the end of his speech is evil madness.
differences.authoritative: The beginning of his talk is folly, and the end of his speech is evil madness.

differences.structured: Yet the fool multiplies words.No one knows what is coming,and who can tell him what will come after him?
differences.authoritative: Yet the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming, and who can tell him what will come after him?

differences.structured: The toil of a fool wearies him,for he does not know the way to the city.
differences.authoritative: The toil of a fool wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.

differences.structured: Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth,and whose princes feast in the morning.
differences.authoritative: Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth, and whose princes feast in the morning.

differences.structured: Blessed are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles,and whose princes feast at the proper time—for strength and not for drunkenness.
differences.authoritative: Blessed are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes feast at the proper time—for strength and not for drunkenness.

differences.structured: Through laziness the roof caves in,and in the hands of the idle, the house leaks.
differences.authoritative: Through laziness the roof caves in, and in the hands of the idle, the house leaks.

differences.structured: A feast is prepared for laughter, and wine makes life merry,but money is the answer for everything.
differences.authoritative: A feast is prepared for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.

differences.structured: Do not curse the king even in your thoughts,or curse the rich even in your bedroom,for a bird of the air may carry your words,and a winged creature may report your speech.
differences.authoritative: Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich even in your bedroom, for a bird of the air may carry your words, and a winged creature may report your speech.

differences.structured: Cast your bread upon the waters,for after many days you will find it again.
differences.authoritative: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.

differences.structured: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight,for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.
differences.authoritative: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.

differences.structured: If the clouds are full,they will pour out rain upon the earth;whether a tree falls to the south or to the north,in the place where it falls, there it will lie.
differences.authoritative: If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.

differences.structured: He who watches the wind will fail to sow,and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.
differences.authoritative: He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.

differences.structured: As you do not know the path of the wind,or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb,so you cannot understand the work of God,the Maker of all things.
differences.authoritative: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.

differences.structured: Sow your seed in the morning,and do not rest your hands in the evening,for you do not know which will succeed,whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.
differences.authoritative: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.

differences.structured: Light is sweet,and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.
differences.authoritative: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.

differences.structured: So if a man lives many years,let him rejoice in them all.But let him remember the days of darkness,for they will be many.Everything to come is futile.
differences.authoritative: So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything to come is futile.

differences.structured: Rejoice, O young man, while you are young,and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth.Walk in the ways of your heartand in the sight of your eyes,but know that for all these thingsGod will bring you to judgment.
differences.authoritative: Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.

differences.structured: So banish sorrow from your heart,and cast off pain from your body,for youth and vigor are fleeting.
differences.authoritative: So banish sorrow from your heart, and cast off pain from your body, for youth and vigor are fleeting.

differences.structured: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth,before the days of adversity comeand the years approach of which you will say,“I find no pleasure in them,”
differences.authoritative: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”

differences.structured: before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened,and the clouds return after the rain,
differences.authoritative: before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened, and the clouds return after the rain,

differences.structured: on the day the keepers of the house trembleand the strong men stoop,when those grinding cease because they are fewand those watching through windows see dimly,
differences.authoritative: on the day the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when those grinding cease because they are few and those watching through windows see dimly,

differences.structured: when the doors to the street are shutand the sound of the mill fades away,when one rises at the sound of a birdand all the daughters of song grow faint,
differences.authoritative: when the doors to the street are shut and the sound of the mill fades away, when one rises at the sound of a bird and all the daughters of song grow faint,

differences.structured: when men fear the heights and dangers of the road,when the almond tree blossoms,the grasshopper loses its spring,and the caper berry shrivels —for then man goes to his eternal homeand mourners walk the streets.
differences.authoritative: when men fear the heights and dangers of the road, when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper loses its spring, and the caper berry shrivels—for then man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets.

differences.structured: Remember Him before the silver cord is snappedand the golden bowl is crushed,before the pitcher is shattered at the springand the wheel is broken at the well,
differences.authoritative: Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel is broken at the well,

differences.structured: before the dust returns to the ground from which it cameand the spirit returns to God who gave it.
differences.authoritative: before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

differences.structured: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher.“Everything is futile!”
differences.authoritative: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”

differences.structured: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth!For your love is more delightful than wine.
differences.authoritative: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is more delightful than wine.

differences.structured: The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing;your name is like perfume poured out.No wonder the maidens adore you.
differences.authoritative: The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing; your name is like perfume poured out. No wonder the maidens adore you.

differences.structured: Take me away with you— let us hurry!May the king bring me to his chambers.We will rejoice and delight in you;we will praise your love more than wine.It is only right that they adore you.
differences.authoritative: Take me away with you—let us hurry! May the king bring me to his chambers. We will rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love more than wine. It is only right that they adore you.

differences.structured: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem,like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
differences.authoritative: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.

differences.structured: Do not stare because I am dark,for the sun has gazed upon me.My mother’s sons were angry with me;they made me a keeper of the vineyards,but my own vineyard I have neglected.
differences.authoritative: Do not stare because I am dark, for the sun has gazed upon me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; they made me a keeper of the vineyards, but my own vineyard I have neglected.

differences.structured: Tell me, O one I love,where do you pasture your sheep?Where do you rest them at midday?Why should I be like a veiled womanbeside the flocks of your companions?
differences.authoritative: Tell me, O one I love, where do you pasture your sheep? Where do you rest them at midday? Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your companions?

differences.structured: If you do not know, O fairest of women,follow the tracks of the flock,and graze your young goatsnear the tents of the shepherds.
differences.authoritative: If you do not know, O fairest of women, follow the tracks of the flock, and graze your young goats near the tents of the shepherds.

differences.structured: I compare you, my darling,to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.
differences.authoritative: I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.

differences.structured: Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments,your neck with strings of jewels.
differences.authoritative: Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.

differences.structured: We will make you ornaments of gold,studded with beads of silver.
differences.authoritative: We will make you ornaments of gold, studded with beads of silver.

differences.structured: While the king was at his table,my perfume spread its fragrance.
differences.authoritative: While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.

differences.structured: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrhresting between my breasts.
differences.authoritative: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.

differences.structured: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossomsin the vineyards of En-gedi.
differences.authoritative: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi.

differences.structured: How beautiful you are, my darling!Oh, how very beautiful!Your eyes are like doves.
differences.authoritative: How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves.

differences.structured: How handsome you are, my beloved!Oh, how delightful!The soft grass is our bed.
differences.authoritative: How handsome you are, my beloved! Oh, how delightful! The soft grass is our bed.

differences.structured: The beams of our house are cedars;our rafters are fragrant firs.
differences.authoritative: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are fragrant firs.

differences.structured: I am a rose of Sharon,a lily of the valley.
differences.authoritative: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valley.

differences.structured: Like a lily among the thornsis my darling among the maidens.
differences.authoritative: Like a lily among the thorns is my darling among the maidens.

differences.structured: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forestis my beloved among the young men.I delight to sit in his shade,and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
differences.authoritative: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.

differences.structured: He has brought me to the house of wine,and his banner over me is love.
differences.authoritative: He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.

differences.structured: Sustain me with raisins;refresh me with apples,for I am faint with love.
differences.authoritative: Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love.

differences.structured: His left hand is under my head,and his right arm embraces me.
differences.authoritative: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.

differences.structured: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure youby the gazelles and does of the field:Do not arouse or awaken loveuntil the time is right.
differences.authoritative: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.

differences.structured: Listen! My beloved approaches.Look! Here he comes,leaping across the mountains,bounding over the hills.
differences.authoritative: Listen! My beloved approaches. Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.

differences.structured: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag.Look, he stands behind our wall,gazing through the windows,peering through the lattice.
differences.authoritative: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.

differences.structured: My beloved calls to me,“Arise, my darling.Come away with me, my beautiful one.
differences.authoritative: My beloved calls to me, “Arise, my darling. Come away with me, my beautiful one.

differences.structured: For now the winter is past;the rain is over and gone.
differences.authoritative: For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.

differences.structured: The flowers have appeared in the countryside;the season of singing has come,and the cooing of turtledovesis heard in our land.
differences.authoritative: The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.

differences.structured: The fig tree ripens its figs;the blossoming vines spread their fragrance.Arise, come away, my darling;come away with me, my beautiful one.”
differences.authoritative: The fig tree ripens its figs; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come away, my darling; come away with me, my beautiful one.”

differences.structured: O my dove in the clefts of the rock,in the crevices of the cliff,let me see your face,let me hear your voice;for your voice is sweet,and your countenance is lovely.
differences.authoritative: O my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the crevices of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely.

differences.structured: My beloved is mine and I am his;he pastures his flock among the lilies.
differences.authoritative: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.

differences.structured: Before the day breaks and shadows flee,turn, my beloved,and be like a gazelleor a young stag on the mountains of Bether.
differences.authoritative: Before the day breaks and shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether.

differences.structured: On my bed at nightI sought the one I love;I sought him,but did not find him.
differences.authoritative: On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.

differences.structured: I will arise now and go about the city,through the streets and squares.I will seek the one I love.So I sought him but did not find him.
differences.authoritative: I will arise now and go about the city, through the streets and squares. I will seek the one I love. So I sought him but did not find him.

differences.structured: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city:“Have you seen the one I love?”
differences.authoritative: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city: “Have you seen the one I love?”

differences.structured: I had just passed them when I found the one I love.I held him and would not let gountil I had brought him to my mother’s house,to the chamber of the one who conceived me.
differences.authoritative: I had just passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.

differences.structured: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure youby the gazelles and does of the field:Do not arouse or awaken loveuntil the time is right.
differences.authoritative: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.

differences.structured: Who is this coming up from the wildernesslike a column of smoke,scented with myrrh and frankincensefrom all the spices of the merchant?
differences.authoritative: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense from all the spices of the merchant?

differences.structured: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage,escorted by sixty of the mightiest men of Israel.
differences.authoritative: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage, escorted by sixty of the mightiest men of Israel.

differences.structured: All are skilled with the sword,experienced in warfare.Each has his sword at his sideprepared for the terror of the night.
differences.authoritative: All are skilled with the sword, experienced in warfare. Each has his sword at his side prepared for the terror of the night.

differences.structured: King Solomon has made his carriageout of the timber of Lebanon.
differences.authoritative: King Solomon has made his carriage out of the timber of Lebanon.

differences.structured: He has made its posts of silver,its base of gold, its seat of purple fabric.Its interior is inlaid with loveby the daughters of Jerusalem.
differences.authoritative: He has made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple fabric. Its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.

differences.structured: Come out, O daughters of Zion,and gaze at King Solomon,wearing the crown with which his mother crowned himon the day of his wedding—the day of his heart’s rejoicing.
differences.authoritative: Come out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze at King Solomon, wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding—the day of his heart’s rejoicing.

differences.structured: How beautiful you are, my darling—how very beautiful!Your eyes are like dovesbehind your veil.Your hair is like a flock of goatsstreaming down Mount Gilead.
differences.authoritative: How beautiful you are, my darling—how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.

differences.structured: Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheepcoming up from the washing;each has its twin,and not one of them is lost.
differences.authoritative: Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.

differences.structured: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon,and your mouth is lovely.Your brow behind your veilis like a slice of pomegranate.
differences.authoritative: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, and your mouth is lovely. Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.

differences.structured: Your neck is like the tower of David,built with rows of stones;on it hang a thousand shields,all of them shields of warriors.
differences.authoritative: Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.

differences.structured: Your breasts are like two fawns,twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.
differences.authoritative: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.

differences.structured: Before the day breaks and the shadows flee,I will make my wayto the mountain of myrrhand to the hill of frankincense.
differences.authoritative: Before the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will make my way to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.

differences.structured: You are altogether beautiful, my darling;in you there is no flaw.
differences.authoritative: You are altogether beautiful, my darling; in you there is no flaw.

differences.structured: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride,come with me from Lebanon!Descend from the peak of Amana,from the summits of Senir and Hermon,from the dens of the lions,from the mountains of the leopards.
differences.authoritative: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon! Descend from the peak of Amana, from the summits of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.

differences.structured: You have captured my heart,my sister, my bride;you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes,with one jewel of your neck.
differences.authoritative: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your neck.

differences.structured: How delightful is your love,my sister, my bride!Your love is much better than wine,and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices.
differences.authoritative: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is much better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices.

differences.structured: Your lips, my bride,drip sweetness like the honeycomb;honey and milk are under your tongue,and the fragrance of your garmentsis like the aroma of Lebanon.
differences.authoritative: Your lips, my bride, drip sweetness like the honeycomb; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the aroma of Lebanon.

differences.structured: My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up,a spring enclosed, a fountain sealed.
differences.authoritative: My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up, a spring enclosed, a fountain sealed.

differences.structured: Your branches are an orchard of pomegranateswith the choicest of fruits, with henna and nard,
differences.authoritative: Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with the choicest of fruits, with henna and nard,

differences.structured: with nard and saffron, with calamus and cinnamon,with every kind of frankincense tree,with myrrh and aloes,with all the finest spices.
differences.authoritative: with nard and saffron, with calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense tree, with myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.

differences.structured: You are a garden spring,a well of fresh waterflowing down from Lebanon.
differences.authoritative: You are a garden spring, a well of fresh water flowing down from Lebanon.

differences.structured: Awake, O north wind,and come, O south wind.Breathe on my gardenand spread the fragrance of its spices.Let my beloved come into his gardenand taste its choicest fruits.
differences.authoritative: Awake, O north wind, and come, O south wind. Breathe on my garden and spread the fragrance of its spices. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its choicest fruits.

differences.structured: I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride;I have gathered my myrrh with my spice.I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey;I have drunk my wine with my milk.Eat, O friends, and drink;drink freely, O beloved.
differences.authoritative: I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends, and drink; drink freely, O beloved.

differences.structured: I sleep, but my heart is awake.A sound! My beloved is knocking:“Open to me, my sister, my darling,my dove, my flawless one.My head is drenched with dew,my hair with the dampness of the night.”
differences.authoritative: I sleep, but my heart is awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”

differences.structured: I have taken off my robe —must I put it back on?I have washed my feet—must I soil them again?
differences.authoritative: I have taken off my robe—must I put it back on? I have washed my feet—must I soil them again?

differences.structured: My beloved put his hand to the latch;my heart pounded for him.
differences.authoritative: My beloved put his hand to the latch; my heart pounded for him.

differences.structured: I rose up to open for my beloved.My hands dripped with myrrh,my fingers with flowing myrrhon the handles of the bolt.
differences.authoritative: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.

differences.structured: I opened for my beloved,but he had turned and gone.My heart sank at his departure.I sought him but did not find him.I called, but he did not answer.
differences.authoritative: I opened for my beloved, but he had turned and gone. My heart sank at his departure. I sought him but did not find him. I called, but he did not answer.

differences.structured: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city.They beat me and bruised me;they took away my cloak,those guardians of the walls.
differences.authoritative: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city. They beat me and bruised me; they took away my cloak, those guardians of the walls.

differences.structured: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you,if you find my beloved,tell him I am sick with love.
differences.authoritative: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you, if you find my beloved, tell him I am sick with love.

differences.structured: How is your beloved better than others,O most beautiful among women?How is your beloved better than another,that you charge us so?
differences.authoritative: How is your beloved better than others, O most beautiful among women? How is your beloved better than another, that you charge us so?

differences.structured: My beloved is dazzling and ruddy,outstanding among ten thousand.
differences.authoritative: My beloved is dazzling and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.

differences.structured: His head is purest gold;his hair is wavy and black as a raven.
differences.authoritative: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.

differences.structured: His eyes are like dovesbeside the streams of water,bathed in milkand mounted like jewels.
differences.authoritative: His eyes are like doves beside the streams of water, bathed in milk and mounted like jewels.

differences.structured: His cheeks are like beds of spice,towers of perfume.His lips are like lilies,dripping with flowing myrrh.
differences.authoritative: His cheeks are like beds of spice, towers of perfume. His lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.

differences.structured: His arms are rods of goldset with beryl.His body is polished ivorybedecked with sapphires.
differences.authoritative: His arms are rods of gold set with beryl. His body is polished ivory bedecked with sapphires.

differences.structured: His legs are pillars of marbleset on bases of pure gold.His appearance is like Lebanon,as majestic as the cedars.
differences.authoritative: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, as majestic as the cedars.

differences.structured: His mouth is most sweet;he is altogether lovely.This is my beloved, and this is my friend,O daughters of Jerusalem.
differences.authoritative: His mouth is most sweet; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

differences.structured: Where has your beloved gone,O most beautiful among women?Which way has he turned?We will seek him with you.
differences.authoritative: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Which way has he turned? We will seek him with you.

differences.structured: My beloved has gone down to his garden,to the beds of spices,to pasture his flock in the gardensand to gather lilies.
differences.authoritative: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.

differences.structured: I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me;he pastures his flock among the lilies.
differences.authoritative: I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me; he pastures his flock among the lilies.

differences.structured: You are as beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah,as lovely as Jerusalem,as majestic as troops with banners.
differences.authoritative: You are as beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem, as majestic as troops with banners.

differences.structured: Turn your eyes away from me,for they have overcome me.Your hair is like a flock of goatsstreaming down from Gilead.
differences.authoritative: Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.

differences.structured: Your teeth are like a flock of sheepcoming up from the washing;each has its twin,and not one of them is lost.
differences.authoritative: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.

differences.structured: Your brow behind your veilis like a slice of pomegranate.
differences.authoritative: Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.

differences.structured: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines,and maidens without number,
differences.authoritative: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and maidens without number,

differences.structured: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique,the favorite of the mother who bore her.The maidens see her and call her blessed;the queens and concubines sing her praises.
differences.authoritative: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, the favorite of the mother who bore her. The maidens see her and call her blessed; the queens and concubines sing her praises.

differences.structured: Who is this who shines like the dawn,as fair as the moon,as bright as the sun,as majestic as the stars in procession?
differences.authoritative: Who is this who shines like the dawn, as fair as the moon, as bright as the sun, as majestic as the stars in procession?

differences.structured: I went down to the walnut groveto see the blossoms of the valley,to see if the vines were buddingor the pomegranates were in bloom.
differences.authoritative: I went down to the walnut grove to see the blossoms of the valley, to see if the vines were budding or the pomegranates were in bloom.

differences.structured: Before I realized it, my desire had set meamong the royal chariots of my people.
differences.authoritative: Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the royal chariots of my people.

differences.structured: Come back, come back, O Shulammite!Come back, come back, that we may gaze upon you.Why do you look at the Shulammite,as on the dance of Mahanaim?
differences.authoritative: Come back, come back, O Shulammite! Come back, come back, that we may gaze upon you. Why do you look at the Shulammite, as on the dance of Mahanaim?

differences.structured: How beautiful are your sandaled feet,O daughter of the prince!The curves of your thighs are like jewels,the handiwork of a master.
differences.authoritative: How beautiful are your sandaled feet, O daughter of the prince! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the handiwork of a master.

differences.structured: Your navel is a rounded goblet;it never lacks blended wine.Your waist is a mound of wheatencircled by the lilies.
differences.authoritative: Your navel is a rounded goblet; it never lacks blended wine. Your waist is a mound of wheat encircled by the lilies.

differences.structured: Your breasts are like two fawns,twins of a gazelle.
differences.authoritative: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.

differences.structured: Your neck is like a towermade of ivory;your eyes are like the pools of Heshbonby the gate of Bath-rabbim;your nose is like the tower of Lebanon,facing toward Damascus.
differences.authoritative: Your neck is like a tower made of ivory; your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim; your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, facing toward Damascus.

differences.structured: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel,the hair of your head like purple threads;the king is captured in your tresses.
differences.authoritative: Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, the hair of your head like purple threads; the king is captured in your tresses.

differences.structured: How fair and pleasant you are,O love, with your delights!
differences.authoritative: How fair and pleasant you are, O love, with your delights!

differences.structured: Your stature is like a palm tree;your breasts are clusters of fruit.
differences.authoritative: Your stature is like a palm tree; your breasts are clusters of fruit.

differences.structured: I said, “I will climb the palm tree;I will take hold of its fruit.”May your breasts be like clusters of the vine,the fragrance of your breath like apples,
differences.authoritative: I said, “I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the fragrance of your breath like apples,

differences.structured: and your mouth like the finest wine.May it flow smoothly to my beloved,gliding gently over lips and teeth.
differences.authoritative: and your mouth like the finest wine. May it flow smoothly to my beloved, gliding gently over lips and teeth.

differences.structured: I belong to my beloved,and his desire is for me.
differences.authoritative: I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.

differences.structured: Come, my beloved,let us go to the countryside;let us spend the night among the wildflowers.
differences.authoritative: Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside; let us spend the night among the wildflowers.

differences.structured: Let us go early to the vineyardsto see if the vine has budded,if the blossom has opened,if the pomegranates are in bloom —there I will give you my love.
differences.authoritative: Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom—there I will give you my love.
