differences.structured: Among all the sons she bore,there is no one to guide her;among all the sons she brought up,there is no one to take her hand.
differences.authoritative: Among all the sons she bore, there is no one to guide her; among all the sons she brought up, there is no one to take her hand.

differences.structured: These pairs have befallen you:devastation and destruction,famine and sword.Who will grieve for you?Who can comfort you?
differences.authoritative: These pairs have befallen you: devastation and destruction, famine and sword. Who will grieve for you? Who can comfort you?

differences.structured: Your sons have fainted;they lie at the head of every street,like an antelope in a net.They are full of the wrath of the LORD,the rebuke of your God.
differences.authoritative: Your sons have fainted; they lie at the head of every street, like an antelope in a net. They are full of the wrath of the LORD, the rebuke of your God.

differences.structured: Therefore now hear this, you afflicted one,drunken, but not with wine.
differences.authoritative: Therefore now hear this, you afflicted one, drunken, but not with wine.

differences.structured: Thus says your Lord, the LORD,even your God, who defends His people:“See, I have removed from your handthe cup of staggering.From that goblet, the cup of My fury,you will never drink again.
differences.authoritative: Thus says your Lord, the LORD, even your God, who defends His people: “See, I have removed from your hand the cup of staggering. From that goblet, the cup of My fury, you will never drink again.

differences.structured: I will place it in the hands of your tormentors,who told you: ‘Lie down, so we can walk over you,’so that you made your back like the ground,like a street to be traversed.”
differences.authoritative: I will place it in the hands of your tormentors, who told you: ‘Lie down, so we can walk over you,’ so that you made your back like the ground, like a street to be traversed.”

differences.structured: Awake, awake,clothe yourself with strength, O Zion!Put on your garments of splendor,O Jerusalem, holy city!For the uncircumcised and uncleanwill no longer enter you.
differences.authoritative: Awake, awake, clothe yourself with strength, O Zion! Put on your garments of splendor, O Jerusalem, holy city! For the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer enter you.

differences.structured: Shake off your dust!Rise up and sit on your throne, O Jerusalem.Remove the chains from your neck,O captive Daughter of Zion.
differences.authoritative: Shake off your dust! Rise up and sit on your throne, O Jerusalem. Remove the chains from your neck, O captive Daughter of Zion.

differences.structured: For this is what the LORD says:“You were sold for nothing,and without money you will be redeemed.”
differences.authoritative: For this is what the LORD says: “You were sold for nothing, and without money you will be redeemed.”

differences.structured: For this is what the Lord GOD says:“At first My people went down to Egypt to live,then Assyria oppressed them without cause.
differences.authoritative: For this is what the Lord GOD says: “At first My people went down to Egypt to live, then Assyria oppressed them without cause.

differences.structured: And now what have I here?declares the LORD.For My people have been taken without cause;those who rule them taunt,declares the LORD,and My name is blasphemed continuallyall day long.
differences.authoritative: And now what have I here? declares the LORD. For My people have been taken without cause; those who rule them taunt, declares the LORD, and My name is blasphemed continually all day long.

differences.structured: Therefore My people will know My name;therefore they will know on that daythat I am He who speaks.Here I am!”
differences.authoritative: Therefore My people will know My name; therefore they will know on that day that I am He who speaks. Here I am!”

differences.structured: How beautiful on the mountainsare the feet of those who bring good news,who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings,who proclaim salvation,who say to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
differences.authoritative: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings, who proclaim salvation, who say to Zion, “Your God reigns!”

differences.structured: Listen! Your watchmen lift up their voices,together they shout for joy.For every eye will seewhen the LORD returns to Zion.
differences.authoritative: Listen! Your watchmen lift up their voices, together they shout for joy. For every eye will see when the LORD returns to Zion.

differences.structured: Break forth in joy, sing together,O ruins of Jerusalem,for the LORD has comforted His people;He has redeemed Jerusalem.
differences.authoritative: Break forth in joy, sing together, O ruins of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted His people; He has redeemed Jerusalem.

differences.structured: The LORD has bared His holy armin the sight of all the nations;all the ends of the earth will seethe salvation of our God.
differences.authoritative: The LORD has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations; all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.

differences.structured: Depart, depart, go out from there!Touch no unclean thing;come out from it, purify yourselves,you who carry the vessels of the LORD.
differences.authoritative: Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch no unclean thing; come out from it, purify yourselves, you who carry the vessels of the LORD.

differences.structured: For you will not leave in a hurrynor flee in haste,for the LORD goes before you,and the God of Israel is your rear guard.
differences.authoritative: For you will not leave in a hurry nor flee in haste, for the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your rear guard.

differences.structured: Behold, My Servant will prosper;He will be raised and lifted up and highly exalted.
differences.authoritative: Behold, My Servant will prosper; He will be raised and lifted up and highly exalted.

differences.structured: Just as many were appalled at Him—His appearance was disfigured beyond that of any man,and His form was marred beyond human likeness—
differences.authoritative: Just as many were appalled at Him—His appearance was disfigured beyond that of any man, and His form was marred beyond human likeness—

differences.structured: so He will sprinkle many nations.Kings will shut their mouths because of Him.For they will see what they have not been told,and they will understand what they have not heard.
differences.authoritative: so He will sprinkle many nations. Kings will shut their mouths because of Him. For they will see what they have not been told, and they will understand what they have not heard.

differences.structured: Who has believed our message?And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?
differences.authoritative: Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?

differences.structured: He grew up before Him like a tender shoot,and like a root out of dry ground.He had no stately form or majesty to attract us,no beauty that we should desire Him.
differences.authoritative: He grew up before Him like a tender shoot, and like a root out of dry ground. He had no stately form or majesty to attract us, no beauty that we should desire Him.

differences.structured: He was despised and rejected by men,a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief.Like one from whom men hide their faces,He was despised, and we esteemed Him not.
differences.authoritative: He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief. Like one from whom men hide their faces, He was despised, and we esteemed Him not.

differences.structured: Surely He took up our infirmitiesand carried our sorrows;yet we considered Him stricken,struck down by God, and afflicted.
differences.authoritative: Surely He took up our infirmities and carried our sorrows; yet we considered Him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.

differences.structured: But He was pierced for our transgressions,He was crushed for our iniquities;the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him,and by His stripes we are healed.
differences.authoritative: But He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed.

differences.structured: We all like sheep have gone astray,each one has turned to his own way;and the LORD has laid upon Himthe iniquity of us all.
differences.authoritative: We all like sheep have gone astray, each one has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all.

differences.structured: He was oppressed and afflicted,yet He did not open His mouth.He was led like a lamb to the slaughter,and as a sheep before her shearers is silent,so He did not open His mouth.
differences.authoritative: He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth. He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is silent, so He did not open His mouth.

differences.structured: By oppression and judgment He was taken away,and who can recount His descendants?For He was cut off from the land of the living;He was stricken for the transgression of My people.
differences.authoritative: By oppression and judgment He was taken away, and who can recount His descendants? For He was cut off from the land of the living; He was stricken for the transgression of My people.

differences.structured: He was assigned a grave with the wicked,and with a rich man in His death,although He had done no violence,nor was any deceit in His mouth.
differences.authoritative: He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in His death, although He had done no violence, nor was any deceit in His mouth.

differences.structured: Yet it was the LORD’s will to crush Himand to cause Him to suffer;and when His soul is made a guilt offering,He will see His offspring, He will prolong His days,and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand.
differences.authoritative: Yet it was the LORD’s will to crush Him and to cause Him to suffer; and when His soul is made a guilt offering, He will see His offspring, He will prolong His days, and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand.

differences.structured: After the anguish of His soul,He will see the light of life and be satisfied.By His knowledge My righteous Servant will justify many,and He will bear their iniquities.
differences.authoritative: After the anguish of His soul, He will see the light of life and be satisfied. By His knowledge My righteous Servant will justify many, and He will bear their iniquities.

differences.structured: Therefore I will allot Him a portion with the great,and He will divide the spoils with the strong,because He has poured out His life unto death,and He was numbered with the transgressors.Yet He bore the sin of manyand made intercession for the transgressors.
differences.authoritative: Therefore I will allot Him a portion with the great, and He will divide the spoils with the strong, because He has poured out His life unto death, and He was numbered with the transgressors. Yet He bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors.

differences.structured: “Shout for joy, O barren woman,who bears no children;break forth in song and cry aloud,you who have never travailed;because more are the children of the desolate womanthan of her who has a husband,”says the LORD.
differences.authoritative: “Shout for joy, O barren woman, who bears no children; break forth in song and cry aloud, you who have never travailed; because more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband,” says the LORD.

differences.structured: “Enlarge the site of your tent,stretch out the curtains of your dwellings,do not hold back.Lengthen your ropesand drive your stakes in deep.
differences.authoritative: “Enlarge the site of your tent, stretch out the curtains of your dwellings, do not hold back. Lengthen your ropes and drive your stakes in deep.

differences.structured: For you will spread out to the right and left;your descendants will dispossess the nationsand inhabit the desolate cities.
differences.authoritative: For you will spread out to the right and left; your descendants will dispossess the nations and inhabit the desolate cities.

differences.structured: Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame;do not be intimidated, for you will not be humiliated.For you will forget the shame of your youthand will remember no more the reproach of your widowhood.
differences.authoritative: Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; do not be intimidated, for you will not be humiliated. For you will forget the shame of your youth and will remember no more the reproach of your widowhood.

differences.structured: For your husband is your Maker —the LORD of Hosts is His name—the Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer;He is called the God of all the earth.
differences.authoritative: For your husband is your Maker—the LORD of Hosts is His name—the Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer; He is called the God of all the earth.

differences.structured: For the LORD has called you back,like a wife deserted and wounded in spirit,like the rejected wife of one’s youth,”says your God.
differences.authoritative: For the LORD has called you back, like a wife deserted and wounded in spirit, like the rejected wife of one’s youth,” says your God.

differences.structured: “For a brief moment I forsook you,but with great compassion I will bring you back.
differences.authoritative: “For a brief moment I forsook you, but with great compassion I will bring you back.

differences.structured: In a surge of angerI hid My face from you for a moment,but with everlasting kindness I will have compassion on you,”says the LORD your Redeemer.
differences.authoritative: In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I will have compassion on you,” says the LORD your Redeemer.

differences.structured: “For to Me this is like the days of Noah,when I swore that the waters of Noahwould never again cover the earth.So I have sworn that I will not be angry with youor rebuke you.
differences.authoritative: “For to Me this is like the days of Noah, when I swore that the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth. So I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.

differences.structured: Though the mountains may be removedand the hills may be shaken,My loving devotion will not depart from you,and My covenant of peace will not be broken,”says the LORD, who has compassion on you.
differences.authoritative: Though the mountains may be removed and the hills may be shaken, My loving devotion will not depart from you, and My covenant of peace will not be broken,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you.

differences.structured: “O afflicted city, lashed by storms,without solace,surely I will set your stones in antimonyand lay your foundations with sapphires.
differences.authoritative: “O afflicted city, lashed by storms, without solace, surely I will set your stones in antimony and lay your foundations with sapphires.

differences.structured: I will make your pinnacles of rubies,your gates of sparkling jewels,and all your walls of precious stones.
differences.authoritative: I will make your pinnacles of rubies, your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.

differences.structured: Then all your sons will be taught by the LORD,and great will be their prosperity.
differences.authoritative: Then all your sons will be taught by the LORD, and great will be their prosperity.

differences.structured: In righteousness you will be established,far from oppression,for you will have no fear.Terror will be far removed,for it will not come near you.
differences.authoritative: In righteousness you will be established, far from oppression, for you will have no fear. Terror will be far removed, for it will not come near you.

differences.structured: If anyone attacks you, it is not from Me;whoever assails you will fall before you.
differences.authoritative: If anyone attacks you, it is not from Me; whoever assails you will fall before you.

differences.structured: Behold, I have created the craftsmanwho fans the coals into flameand forges a weapon fit for its task;and I have created the destroyerto wreak havoc.
differences.authoritative: Behold, I have created the craftsman who fans the coals into flame and forges a weapon fit for its task; and I have created the destroyer to wreak havoc.

differences.structured: No weapon formed against you shall prosper,and you will refute every tongue that accuses you.This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD,and their vindication is from Me,”declares the LORD.
differences.authoritative: No weapon formed against you shall prosper, and you will refute every tongue that accuses you. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their vindication is from Me,” declares the LORD.

differences.structured: “Come, all you who are thirsty,come to the waters;and you without money,come, buy, and eat!Come, buy wine and milkwithout money and without cost!
differences.authoritative: “Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters; and you without money, come, buy, and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost!

differences.structured: Why spend money on that which is not bread,and your labor on that which does not satisfy?Listen carefully to Me, and eat what is good,and your soul will delight in the richest of foods.
differences.authoritative: Why spend money on that which is not bread, and your labor on that which does not satisfy? Listen carefully to Me, and eat what is good, and your soul will delight in the richest of foods.

differences.structured: Incline your ear and come to Me;listen, so that your soul may live.I will make with you an everlasting covenant —My loving devotion promised to David.
differences.authoritative: Incline your ear and come to Me; listen, so that your soul may live. I will make with you an everlasting covenant—My loving devotion promised to David.

differences.structured: Behold, I have made him a witness to the nations,a leader and commander of the peoples.
differences.authoritative: Behold, I have made him a witness to the nations, a leader and commander of the peoples.

differences.structured: Surely you will summon a nation you do not know,and nations who do not know you will run to you.For the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel,has bestowed glory on you.”
differences.authoritative: Surely you will summon a nation you do not know, and nations who do not know you will run to you. For the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, has bestowed glory on you.”

differences.structured: Seek the LORD while He may be found;call on Him while He is near.
differences.authoritative: Seek the LORD while He may be found; call on Him while He is near.

differences.structured: Let the wicked man forsake his wayand the unrighteous man his thoughts;let him return to the LORD,that He may have compassion,and to our God,for He will freely pardon.
differences.authoritative: Let the wicked man forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the LORD, that He may have compassion, and to our God, for He will freely pardon.

differences.structured: “For My thoughts are not your thoughts,neither are your ways My ways,”declares the LORD.
differences.authoritative: “For My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways,” declares the LORD.

differences.structured: “For as the heavens are higher than the earth,so My ways are higher than your waysand My thoughts than your thoughts.
differences.authoritative: “For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts.

differences.structured: For just as rain and snow fall from heavenand do not return without watering the earth,making it bud and sprout,and providing seed to sow and food to eat,
differences.authoritative: For just as rain and snow fall from heaven and do not return without watering the earth, making it bud and sprout, and providing seed to sow and food to eat,

differences.structured: so My word that proceeds from My mouthwill not return to Me empty,but it will accomplish what I please,and it will prosper where I send it.
differences.authoritative: so My word that proceeds from My mouth will not return to Me empty, but it will accomplish what I please, and it will prosper where I send it.

differences.structured: You will indeed go out with joyand be led forth in peace;the mountains and hills will burst into song before you,and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
differences.authoritative: You will indeed go out with joy and be led forth in peace; the mountains and hills will burst into song before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.

differences.structured: Instead of the thornbush, the cypress will grow,and instead of the brier, the myrtle will spring up;this will make a name for the LORD,an everlasting sign, never to be destroyed.”
differences.authoritative: Instead of the thornbush, the cypress will grow, and instead of the brier, the myrtle will spring up; this will make a name for the LORD, an everlasting sign, never to be destroyed.”

differences.structured: This is what the LORD says:“Maintain justice and do what is right,for My salvation is coming soon,and My righteousness will be revealed.
differences.authoritative: This is what the LORD says: “Maintain justice and do what is right, for My salvation is coming soon, and My righteousness will be revealed.

differences.structured: Blessed is the man who does this,and the son of man who holds it fast,who keeps the Sabbath without profaning itand keeps his hand from doing any evil.”
differences.authoritative: Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds it fast, who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.”

differences.authoritative: Let no foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, “The LORD will utterly exclude me from His people.” And let the eunuch not say, “I am but a dry tree.”

differences.structured: For this is what the LORD says:“To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths,who choose what pleases Meand hold fast to My covenant —
differences.authoritative: For this is what the LORD says: “To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths, who choose what pleases Me and hold fast to My covenant—

differences.structured: I will give them, in My house and within My walls,a memorial and a namebetter than that of sons and daughters.I will give them an everlasting namethat will not be cut off.
differences.authoritative: I will give them, in My house and within My walls, a memorial and a name better than that of sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will not be cut off.

differences.structured: And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORDto minister to Him,to love the name of the LORD,and to be His servants —all who keep the Sabbath without profaning itand who hold fast to My covenant—
differences.authoritative: And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to minister to Him, to love the name of the LORD, and to be His servants—all who keep the Sabbath without profaning it and who hold fast to My covenant—

differences.structured: I will bring them to My holy mountainand make them joyful in My house of prayer.Their burnt offerings and sacrificeswill be accepted on My altar,for My house will be called a house of prayerfor all the nations.”
differences.authoritative: I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on My altar, for My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.”

differences.structured: Thus declares the Lord GOD,who gathers the dispersed of Israel:“I will gather to them still othersbesides those already gathered.”

differences.structured: Come, all you beasts of the field;eat greedily, all you beasts of the forest.
differences.authoritative: Come, all you beasts of the field; eat greedily, all you beasts of the forest.

differences.authoritative: Israel’s watchmen are blind, they are all oblivious; they are all mute dogs, they cannot bark; they are dreamers lying around, loving to slumber.

differences.authoritative: Like ravenous dogs, they are never satisfied. They are shepherds with no discernment; they all turn to their own way, each one seeking his own gain:

differences.structured: “Come, let me get the wine,let us imbibe the strong drink,and tomorrow will be like today,only far better!”
differences.authoritative: “Come, let me get the wine, let us imbibe the strong drink, and tomorrow will be like today, only far better!”

differences.structured: The righteous perish,and no one takes it to heart;devout men are taken away,while no one considersthat the righteous are taken awayfrom the presence of evil.
differences.authoritative: The righteous perish, and no one takes it to heart; devout men are taken away, while no one considers that the righteous are taken away from the presence of evil.

differences.structured: Those who walk uprightly enter into peace;they find rest, lying down in death.
differences.authoritative: Those who walk uprightly enter into peace; they find rest, lying down in death.

differences.structured: “But come here, you sons of a sorceress,you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes!
differences.authoritative: “But come here, you sons of a sorceress, you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes!

differences.authoritative: On a high and lofty hill you have made your bed, and there you went up to offer sacrifices.

differences.authoritative: You went to Molech with oil and multiplied your perfumes. You have sent your envoys a great distance; you have descended even to Sheol itself.

differences.structured: You are wearied by your many journeys,but you did not say, “There is no hope!”You found renewal of your strength;therefore you did not grow weak.
differences.authoritative: You are wearied by your many journeys, but you did not say, “There is no hope!” You found renewal of your strength; therefore you did not grow weak.

differences.structured: Whom have you dreaded and feared,so that you lied and failedto remember Me or take this to heart?Is it not because I have long been silentthat you do not fear Me?
differences.authoritative: Whom have you dreaded and feared, so that you lied and failed to remember Me or take this to heart? Is it not because I have long been silent that you do not fear Me?

differences.structured: I will expose your righteousness and your works,and they will not profit you.

differences.authoritative: bringing praise to their lips. Peace, peace to those far and near,” says the LORD, “and I will heal them.”

differences.authoritative: Then I will return to My place until they admit their guilt and seek My face; in their affliction they will earnestly seek Me.”

differences.structured: Come, let us return to the LORD.For He has torn us to pieces,but He will heal us;He has wounded us,but He will bind up our wounds.
differences.authoritative: Come, let us return to the LORD. For He has torn us to pieces, but He will heal us; He has wounded us, but He will bind up our wounds.

differences.structured: After two days He will revive us;on the third day He will raise us up,that we may live in His presence.
differences.authoritative: After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up, that we may live in His presence.

differences.structured: So let us know —let us press on to know the LORD.As surely as the sun rises,He will appear;He will come to us like the rain,like the spring showers that water the earth.
differences.authoritative: So let us know—let us press on to know the LORD. As surely as the sun rises, He will appear; He will come to us like the rain, like the spring showers that water the earth.

differences.structured: What shall I do with you, O Ephraim?What shall I do with you, O Judah?For your loyalty is like a morning mist,like the early dew that vanishes.
differences.authoritative: What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah? For your loyalty is like a morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes.

differences.structured: Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets;I have slain them by the words of My mouth,and My judgments go forth like lightning.
differences.authoritative: Therefore I have hewn them by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of My mouth, and My judgments go forth like lightning.

differences.structured: For I desire mercy, not sacrifice,and the knowledge of Godrather than burnt offerings.
differences.authoritative: For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.

differences.structured: But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant;there they were unfaithful to Me.
differences.authoritative: But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they were unfaithful to Me.

differences.structured: Gilead is a city of evildoers,tracked with footprints of blood.
differences.authoritative: Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with footprints of blood.

differences.structured: Like raiders who lie in ambush,so does a band of priests;they murder on the way to Shechem;surely they have committed atrocities.
differences.authoritative: Like raiders who lie in ambush, so does a band of priests; they murder on the way to Shechem; surely they have committed atrocities.

differences.structured: In the house of IsraelI have seen a horrible thing:Ephraim practices prostitution there,and Israel is defiled.
differences.authoritative: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: Ephraim practices prostitution there, and Israel is defiled.

differences.structured: Also for you, O Judah,a harvest is appointed,when I restoreMy people from captivity.
differences.authoritative: Also for you, O Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I restore My people from captivity.

differences.structured: When I heal Israel,the iniquity of Ephraim will be exposed,as well as the crimes of Samaria.For they practice deceit and thieves break in;bandits raid in the streets.
differences.authoritative: When I heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim will be exposed, as well as the crimes of Samaria. For they practice deceit and thieves break in; bandits raid in the streets.

differences.structured: But they fail to consider in their heartsthat I remember all their evil.Now their deeds are all around them;they are before My face.
differences.authoritative: But they fail to consider in their hearts that I remember all their evil. Now their deeds are all around them; they are before My face.

differences.structured: They delight the king with their evil,and the princes with their lies.
differences.authoritative: They delight the king with their evil, and the princes with their lies.

differences.structured: They are all adulterers,like an oven heated by a bakerwho needs not stoke the firefrom the kneading to the rising of the dough.
differences.authoritative: They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker who needs not stoke the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough.

differences.structured: The princes are inflamed with wineon the day of our king;so he joins handswith those who mock him.
differences.authoritative: The princes are inflamed with wine on the day of our king; so he joins hands with those who mock him.

differences.structured: For they prepare their heart like an ovenwhile they lie in wait;all night their anger smolders;in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
differences.authoritative: For they prepare their heart like an oven while they lie in wait; all night their anger smolders; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.

differences.structured: All of them are hot as an oven,and they devour their rulers.All their kings fall;not one of them calls upon Me.
differences.authoritative: All of them are hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers. All their kings fall; not one of them calls upon Me.

differences.structured: Ephraim mixes with the nations;Ephraim is an unturned cake.
differences.authoritative: Ephraim mixes with the nations; Ephraim is an unturned cake.

differences.structured: Foreigners consume his strength,but he does not notice.Even his hair is streaked with gray,but he does not know.
differences.authoritative: Foreigners consume his strength, but he does not notice. Even his hair is streaked with gray, but he does not know.

differences.structured: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them,yet they do not return to the LORD their God;despite all this, they do not seek Him.
differences.authoritative: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them, yet they do not return to the LORD their God; despite all this, they do not seek Him.

differences.structured: So Ephraim has become like a silly, senseless dove —calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.
differences.authoritative: So Ephraim has become like a silly, senseless dove—calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.

differences.structured: As they go, I will spread My net over them;I will bring them down like birds of the air.I will chastise themwhen I hear them flocking together.
differences.authoritative: As they go, I will spread My net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the air. I will chastise them when I hear them flocking together.

differences.structured: Woe to them, for they have strayed from Me!Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against Me!Though I would redeem them,they speak lies against Me.
differences.authoritative: Woe to them, for they have strayed from Me! Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against Me! Though I would redeem them, they speak lies against Me.

differences.structured: They do not cry out to Me from their heartswhen they wail upon their beds.They slash themselves for grain and new wine,but turn away from Me.
differences.authoritative: They do not cry out to Me from their hearts when they wail upon their beds. They slash themselves for grain and new wine, but turn away from Me.

differences.structured: Although I trained and strengthened their arms,they plot evil against Me.
differences.authoritative: Although I trained and strengthened their arms, they plot evil against Me.

differences.structured: They turn, but not to the Most High;they are like a faulty bow.Their leaders will fall by the swordfor the cursing of their tongue;for this they will be ridiculedin the land of Egypt.
differences.authoritative: They turn, but not to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow. Their leaders will fall by the sword for the cursing of their tongue; for this they will be ridiculed in the land of Egypt.

differences.structured: Put the ram’s horn to your lips!An eagle looms over the house of the LORD,because the people have transgressed My covenantand rebelled against My law.
differences.authoritative: Put the ram’s horn to your lips! An eagle looms over the house of the LORD, because the people have transgressed My covenant and rebelled against My law.

differences.structured: Israel cries out to Me,“O our God, we know You!”
differences.authoritative: Israel cries out to Me, “O our God, we know You!”

differences.structured: But Israel has rejected good;an enemy will pursue him.
differences.authoritative: But Israel has rejected good; an enemy will pursue him.

differences.structured: They set up kings, but not by Me.They make princes, but without My approval.With their silver and gold they make themselves idols,to their own destruction.
differences.authoritative: They set up kings, but not by Me. They make princes, but without My approval. With their silver and gold they make themselves idols, to their own destruction.

differences.structured: He has rejected your calf, O Samaria.My anger burns against them.How long will they beincapable of innocence?
differences.authoritative: He has rejected your calf, O Samaria. My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?

differences.structured: For this thing is from Israel—a craftsman made it, and it is not God.It will be broken to pieces,that calf of Samaria.
differences.authoritative: For this thing is from Israel—a craftsman made it, and it is not God. It will be broken to pieces, that calf of Samaria.

differences.structured: For they sow the wind,and they shall reap the whirlwind.There is no standing grain;what sprouts fails to yield flour.Even if it should produce,the foreigners would swallow it up.
differences.authoritative: For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind. There is no standing grain; what sprouts fails to yield flour. Even if it should produce, the foreigners would swallow it up.

differences.structured: Israel is swallowed up!Now they are among the nationslike a worthless vessel.
differences.authoritative: Israel is swallowed up! Now they are among the nations like a worthless vessel.

differences.structured: For they have gone up to Assyrialike a wild donkey on its own.Ephraim has hired lovers.
differences.authoritative: For they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey on its own. Ephraim has hired lovers.

differences.structured: Though they hire allies among the nations,I will now round them up,and they will begin to diminishunder the oppression of the king of princes.
differences.authoritative: Though they hire allies among the nations, I will now round them up, and they will begin to diminish under the oppression of the king of princes.

differences.structured: Though Ephraim multiplied the altars for sin,they became his altars for sinning.
differences.authoritative: Though Ephraim multiplied the altars for sin, they became his altars for sinning.

differences.structured: Though I wrote for them the great things of My law,they regarded them as something strange.
differences.authoritative: Though I wrote for them the great things of My law, they regarded them as something strange.

differences.structured: Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to Me,and though they eat the meat,the LORD does not accept them.Now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins:They will return to Egypt.
differences.authoritative: Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to Me, and though they eat the meat, the LORD does not accept them. Now He will remember their iniquity and punish their sins: They will return to Egypt.

differences.structured: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces;Judah has multiplied its fortified cities.But I will send fire upon their cities,and it will consume their citadels.
differences.authoritative: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; Judah has multiplied its fortified cities. But I will send fire upon their cities, and it will consume their citadels.

differences.structured: Do not rejoice, O Israel,with exultation like the nations,for you have played the harlot against your God;you have made love for hire on every threshing floor.
differences.authoritative: Do not rejoice, O Israel, with exultation like the nations, for you have played the harlot against your God; you have made love for hire on every threshing floor.

differences.structured: The threshing floor and winepress will not feed them,and the new wine will fail them.
differences.authoritative: The threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail them.

differences.structured: They will not remainin the land of the LORD;Ephraim will return to Egyptand eat unclean food in Assyria.
differences.authoritative: They will not remain in the land of the LORD; Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria.

differences.structured: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD,and their sacrifices will not please Him,but will be to them like the bread of mourners;all who eat will be defiled.For their bread will be for themselves;it will not enter the house of the LORD.
differences.authoritative: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please Him, but will be to them like the bread of mourners; all who eat will be defiled. For their bread will be for themselves; it will not enter the house of the LORD.

differences.structured: What will you do on the appointed day,on the day of the LORD’s feast?
differences.authoritative: What will you do on the appointed day, on the day of the LORD’s feast?

differences.structured: For even if they flee destruction,Egypt will gather themand Memphis will bury them.Their precious silver will be taken over by thistles,and thorns will overrun their tents.
differences.authoritative: For even if they flee destruction, Egypt will gather them and Memphis will bury them. Their precious silver will be taken over by thistles, and thorns will overrun their tents.

differences.structured: The days of punishment have come;the days of retribution have arrived —let Israel know it.The prophet is called a fool,and the inspired man insane,because of the greatnessof your iniquity and hostility.
differences.authoritative: The days of punishment have come; the days of retribution have arrived—let Israel know it. The prophet is called a fool, and the inspired man insane, because of the greatness of your iniquity and hostility.

differences.structured: The prophet is Ephraim’s watchman,along with my God,yet the snare of the fowler lies on all his paths.Hostility is in the house of his God!
differences.authoritative: The prophet is Ephraim’s watchman, along with my God, yet the snare of the fowler lies on all his paths. Hostility is in the house of his God!

differences.structured: They have deeply corrupted themselvesas in the days of Gibeah;He will remember their guilt;He will punish their sins.
differences.authoritative: They have deeply corrupted themselves as in the days of Gibeah; He will remember their guilt; He will punish their sins.

differences.structured: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness.I saw your fathers as the firstfruitsof the fig tree in its first season.But they went to Baal-peor,and consecrated themselves to Shame;so they became as detestableas the thing they loved.
differences.authoritative: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers as the firstfruits of the fig tree in its first season. But they went to Baal-peor, and consecrated themselves to Shame; so they became as detestable as the thing they loved.

differences.structured: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird,with no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception.
differences.authoritative: Ephraim’s glory will fly away like a bird, with no birth, no pregnancy, and no conception.

differences.structured: Even if they raise their children,I will bereave them of each one.Yes, woe be to themwhen I turn away from them!
differences.authoritative: Even if they raise their children, I will bereave them of each one. Yes, woe be to them when I turn away from them!

differences.structured: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre,planted in a meadow.But Ephraim will bring outhis children for slaughter.
differences.authoritative: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a meadow. But Ephraim will bring out his children for slaughter.

differences.structured: Give them, O LORD—what will You give?Give them wombs that miscarryand breasts that dry up!
differences.authoritative: Give them, O LORD—what will You give? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that dry up!

differences.structured: All their evil appears at Gilgal,for there I hated them.I will drive them from My housefor the wickedness of their deeds.I will no longer love them;all their leaders are rebellious.
differences.authoritative: All their evil appears at Gilgal, for there I hated them. I will drive them from My house for the wickedness of their deeds. I will no longer love them; all their leaders are rebellious.

differences.structured: Ephraim is struck down;their root is withered;they cannot bear fruit.Even if they bear children,I will slay the darlings of their wombs.
differences.authoritative: Ephraim is struck down; their root is withered; they cannot bear fruit. Even if they bear children, I will slay the darlings of their wombs.

differences.structured: My God will reject thembecause they have not obeyed Him;and they shall be wanderersamong the nations.
differences.authoritative: My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him; and they shall be wanderers among the nations.

differences.structured: Israel was a luxuriant vine,yielding fruit for himself.The more his fruit increased,the more he increased the altars.The better his land produced,the better he made the sacred pillars.
differences.authoritative: Israel was a luxuriant vine, yielding fruit for himself. The more his fruit increased, the more he increased the altars. The better his land produced, the better he made the sacred pillars.

differences.structured: Their hearts are devious;now they must bear their guilt.The LORD will break down their altarsand demolish their sacred pillars.
differences.authoritative: Their hearts are devious; now they must bear their guilt. The LORD will break down their altars and demolish their sacred pillars.

differences.structured: Surely now they will say,“We have no king,for we do not revere the LORD.What can a king do for us?”
differences.authoritative: Surely now they will say, “We have no king, for we do not revere the LORD. What can a king do for us?”

differences.structured: They speak mere words;with false oaths they make covenants.So judgment springs uplike poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.
differences.authoritative: They speak mere words; with false oaths they make covenants. So judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.

differences.structured: The people of Samaria will fearfor the calf of Beth-aven.Indeed, its people will mourn over itwith its idolatrous priests —those who rejoiced in its glory —for it has been taken from them into exile.
differences.authoritative: The people of Samaria will fear for the calf of Beth-aven. Indeed, its people will mourn over it with its idolatrous priests—those who rejoiced in its glory—for it has been taken from them into exile.

differences.structured: Yes, it will be carried to Assyriaas tribute to the great king.Ephraim will be seized with shame;Israel will be ashamed of its wooden idols.
differences.authoritative: Yes, it will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the great king. Ephraim will be seized with shame; Israel will be ashamed of its wooden idols.

differences.structured: Samaria will be carried off with her kinglike a twig on the surface of the water.
differences.authoritative: Samaria will be carried off with her king like a twig on the surface of the water.

differences.structured: The high places of Aven will be destroyed—it is the sin of Israel;thorns and thistles will overgrow their altars.Then they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!”and to the hills, “Fall on us!”
differences.authoritative: The high places of Aven will be destroyed—it is the sin of Israel; thorns and thistles will overgrow their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall on us!”

differences.structured: Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel,and there you have remained.Did not the battle in Gibeahovertake the sons of iniquity?
differences.authoritative: Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel, and there you have remained. Did not the battle in Gibeah overtake the sons of iniquity?

differences.structured: I will chasten them when I please;nations will be gathered against themto put them in bondagefor their double transgression.
differences.authoritative: I will chasten them when I please; nations will be gathered against them to put them in bondage for their double transgression.

differences.structured: Ephraim is a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh;but I will place a yoke on her fair neck.I will harness Ephraim, Judah will plow,and Jacob will break the hard ground.
differences.authoritative: Ephraim is a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh; but I will place a yoke on her fair neck. I will harness Ephraim, Judah will plow, and Jacob will break the hard ground.

differences.structured: Sow for yourselves righteousnessand reap the fruit of loving devotion;break up your unplowed ground.For it is time to seek the LORDuntil He comes and sends righteousnessupon you like rain.
differences.authoritative: Sow for yourselves righteousness and reap the fruit of loving devotion; break up your unplowed ground. For it is time to seek the LORD until He comes and sends righteousness upon you like rain.

differences.structured: You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice;you have eaten the fruit of lies.Because you have trusted in your own wayand in the multitude of your mighty men,
differences.authoritative: You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of lies. Because you have trusted in your own way and in the multitude of your mighty men,

differences.structured: the roar of battle will rise against your people,so that all your fortresses will be demolishedas Shalman devastated Beth-arbelin the day of battle,when mothers were dashed to piecesalong with their children.
differences.authoritative: the roar of battle will rise against your people, so that all your fortresses will be demolished as Shalman devastated Beth-arbel in the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to pieces along with their children.

differences.structured: Thus it will be done to you, O Bethel,because of your great wickedness.When the day dawns,the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.
differences.authoritative: Thus it will be done to you, O Bethel, because of your great wickedness. When the day dawns, the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.

differences.structured: When Israel was a child, I loved him,and out of Egypt I called My son.
differences.authoritative: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called My son.

differences.structured: But the more I called Israel,the farther they departed from Me.They sacrificed to the Baalsand burned incense to carved images.
differences.authoritative: But the more I called Israel, the farther they departed from Me. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.

differences.structured: It was I who taught Ephraim to walk,taking them by the arms,but they never realizedthat it was I who healed them.
differences.authoritative: It was I who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by the arms, but they never realized that it was I who healed them.

differences.structured: I led them with cords of kindness,with ropes of love;I lifted the yoke from their necksand bent down to feed them.
differences.authoritative: I led them with cords of kindness, with ropes of love; I lifted the yoke from their necks and bent down to feed them.

differences.structured: Will they not return to the land of Egyptand be ruled by Assyriabecause they refused to repent?
differences.authoritative: Will they not return to the land of Egypt and be ruled by Assyria because they refused to repent?

differences.structured: A sword will flash through their cities;it will destroy the bars of their gatesand consume them in their own plans.
differences.authoritative: A sword will flash through their cities; it will destroy the bars of their gates and consume them in their own plans.

differences.structured: My people are bent on turning from Me.Though they call to the Most High,He will by no means exalt them.
differences.authoritative: My people are bent on turning from Me. Though they call to the Most High, He will by no means exalt them.

differences.structured: How could I give you up, O Ephraim?How could I surrender you, O Israel?How could I make you like Admah?How could I treat you like Zeboiim?My heart is turned within Me;My compassion is stirred!
differences.authoritative: How could I give you up, O Ephraim? How could I surrender you, O Israel? How could I make you like Admah? How could I treat you like Zeboiim? My heart is turned within Me; My compassion is stirred!

differences.structured: I will not execute the full fury of My anger;I will not destroy Ephraim again.For I am God and not man —the Holy One among you —and I will not come in wrath.
differences.authoritative: I will not execute the full fury of My anger; I will not destroy Ephraim again. For I am God and not man—the Holy One among you—and I will not come in wrath.

differences.structured: They will walk after the LORD;He will roar like a lion.When He roars,His children will come trembling from the west.
differences.authoritative: They will walk after the LORD; He will roar like a lion. When He roars, His children will come trembling from the west.

differences.structured: They will come trembling like birds from Egyptand like doves from the land of Assyria.Then I will settle them in their homes,declares the LORD.
differences.authoritative: They will come trembling like birds from Egypt and like doves from the land of Assyria. Then I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD.

differences.structured: Ephraim surrounds Me with lies,the house of Israel with deceit;but Judah still walks with Godand is faithful to the Holy One.
differences.authoritative: Ephraim surrounds Me with lies, the house of Israel with deceit; but Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One.

differences.structured: Ephraim feeds on the windand pursues the east wind all day long;he multiplies lies and violence;he makes a covenant with Assyriaand sends olive oil to Egypt.
differences.authoritative: Ephraim feeds on the wind and pursues the east wind all day long; he multiplies lies and violence; he makes a covenant with Assyria and sends olive oil to Egypt.

differences.structured: The LORD has a charge to bring against Judah.He will punish Jacob according to his waysand repay him according to his deeds.
differences.authoritative: The LORD has a charge to bring against Judah. He will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.

differences.structured: In the womb he grasped his brother’s heel,and in his vigor he wrestled with God.
differences.authoritative: In the womb he grasped his brother’s heel, and in his vigor he wrestled with God.

differences.structured: Yes, he struggled with the angel and prevailed;he wept and sought His favor;he found Him at Betheland spoke with Him there —
differences.authoritative: Yes, he struggled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and sought His favor; he found Him at Bethel and spoke with Him there—

differences.structured: the LORD God of Hosts,the LORD is His name of renown.
differences.authoritative: the LORD God of Hosts, the LORD is His name of renown.

differences.structured: But you must return to your God;maintain love and justice,and always wait on your God.
differences.authoritative: But you must return to your God; maintain love and justice, and always wait on your God.

differences.structured: A merchant loves to defraudwith dishonest scales in his hands.
differences.authoritative: A merchant loves to defraud with dishonest scales in his hands.

differences.structured: And Ephraim boasts: “How rich I have become!I have found wealth for myself.In all my labors, they can find in meno iniquity that is sinful.”
differences.authoritative: And Ephraim boasts: “How rich I have become! I have found wealth for myself. In all my labors, they can find in me no iniquity that is sinful.”

differences.structured: But I am the LORD your Godever since the land of Egypt.I will again make you dwell in tents,as in the days of the appointed feast.
differences.authoritative: But I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt. I will again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast.

differences.structured: I spoke through the prophetsand multiplied their visions;I gave parables through the prophets.
differences.authoritative: I spoke through the prophets and multiplied their visions; I gave parables through the prophets.

differences.structured: Is there iniquity in Gilead?They will surely come to nothing.Do they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal?Indeed, their altars will be heaps of stonesin the furrows of the field.
differences.authoritative: Is there iniquity in Gilead? They will surely come to nothing. Do they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal? Indeed, their altars will be heaps of stones in the furrows of the field.

differences.structured: Jacob fled to the land of Aramand Israel worked for a wife —for a wife he tended sheep.
differences.authoritative: Jacob fled to the land of Aram and Israel worked for a wife—for a wife he tended sheep.

differences.structured: But by a prophet the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt,and by a prophet he was preserved.
differences.authoritative: But by a prophet the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was preserved.

differences.structured: Ephraim has provoked bitter anger,so his Lord will leave his bloodguilt upon himand repay him for his contempt.
differences.authoritative: Ephraim has provoked bitter anger, so his Lord will leave his bloodguilt upon him and repay him for his contempt.

differences.structured: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling;he was exalted in Israel.But he incurred guilt through Baal,and he died.
differences.authoritative: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he incurred guilt through Baal, and he died.

differences.structured: Now they sin more and moreand make for themselves cast images,idols skillfully made from their silver,all of them the work of craftsmen.People say of them,“They offer human sacrificeand kiss the calves!”
differences.authoritative: Now they sin more and more and make for themselves cast images, idols skillfully made from their silver, all of them the work of craftsmen. People say of them, “They offer human sacrifice and kiss the calves!”

differences.structured: Therefore they will be like the morning mist,like the early dew that vanishes,like chaff blown from a threshing floor,like smoke through an open window.
differences.authoritative: Therefore they will be like the morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes, like chaff blown from a threshing floor, like smoke through an open window.

differences.structured: Yet I am the LORD your Godever since the land of Egypt;you know no God but Me,for there is no Savior besides Me.
differences.authoritative: Yet I am the LORD your God ever since the land of Egypt; you know no God but Me, for there is no Savior besides Me.

differences.structured: I knew you in the wilderness,in the land of drought.
differences.authoritative: I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of drought.

differences.structured: When they had pasture,they became satisfied;when they were satisfied,their hearts became proud,and as a result they forgot Me.
